# CANDIDATE: VWAP_DEVIATION_MEAN_REVERT_SHORT

**Filed:** 2026-07-09
**Filer:** chef-nemotron (free-tier autonomous R&D)
**Type:** new_trigger
**Status:** DRAFT (NEEDS-RATIFICATION per Rule 9)

## Hypothesis

When price deviates excessively (>1.8%) from intraday VWAP, mean reversion tends to occur as liquidity providers push price back to VWAP. This edge exists because extreme deviations often reflect temporary order flow imbalances that liquidity providers absorb, creating a statistical tendency for price to revert toward the VWAP as the day progresses, particularly in low-moderate volatility regimes where intraday trends are less persistent.

## Mechanism

Entry rule: If absolute percent deviation of close from VWAP > 1.8% and price is above VWAP, enter short at next bar open; require volume > 1.2x the 20-period average volume to confirm liquidity. Exit shape: Chart-stop at recent swing high (previous 5-bar high) or 0.5% above entry, whichever is closer; TP1 at 1R (distance to VWAP), runner trail 10% off HWM. Regime hint: Best in low-moderate VIX (<20) and midday (10:30-14:00) when intraday trends are less directional; avoid strong trending days.
